specification.title: A unique violation is caught inside the transaction, which then ends normally
steps: Start a transaction with the framework's ordinary transaction API.
Write the marker `tx`, and make sure the write was sent to PostgreSQL.
Checkpoint `after-write`: report pg_current_xact_id() and pg_backend_pid(), read through the transaction's own connection.
Insert the value 'taken' into uniq through the framework's ordinary write API. It fails with unique_violation (23505). Catch the error and continue.
Checkpoint `before-end`: report the same backend PID. The transaction is aborted, so it cannot run queries; the runner confirms the aborted state server-side.
End the transaction normally, so that the framework sends COMMIT.

invariants.statement: When PostgreSQL has aborted the transaction before it ends, so that its COMMIT is answered with ROLLBACK, the API does not report a successful commit.

execution.description: TypeORM's defaults, with the managed transaction API ds.transaction(callback).

server.version: PostgreSQL 18.6 (Debian 18.6-1.pgdg13+2) on aarch64-unknown-linux-gnu, compiled by gcc (Debian 14.2.0-19) 14.2.0, 64-bit

fault.mechanism: A unique_violation raised by PostgreSQL inside the transaction, and caught by the application.
fault.injection_point: After the first write, before the transaction ends.
fault.preconditions: The row 'taken' already exists in uniq (fixture).
fault.expected_server: The failed statement aborts the transaction. PostgreSQL answers the later COMMIT with the command tag ROLLBACK, without an error, and commits nothing.
fault.expected_client: The driver receives the command tag ROLLBACK as the reply to COMMIT.

knowledge: The outcome reaches the client: PostgreSQL's reply to COMMIT carries the command tag ROLLBACK.

api_outcome.contract: In TypeORM 1.1.2, ds.transaction(callback) (EntityManager.transaction) starts a transaction, runs the callback, calls commitTransaction() and returns the callback's result; if the callback throws, it calls rollbackTransaction(), ignores any rollback error, and rethrows (entity-manager/EntityManager.js). A resolved call is TypeORM's report that the transaction committed.

violation.message: duplicate key value violates unique constraint "uniq_code_key"

evaluation.reason: TX-01A.1 violated: the API reported: committed

preconditions.description: the duplicate insert failed with unique_violation (23505), as reported by the adapter
the server-side transaction was aborted before it ended (pg_stat_activity at before-end)
PostgreSQL did not commit the transaction
